subject: Request: KEK sealing & rotation chronology for CrestBank SIG review
messages:
From: Laura Mills <laura.mills@crestbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: sig@crestbank.com
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: KEK sealing & rotation chronology

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of CrestBank's SIG/QAR review we need an evidence package for Redwood's key encryption key (KEK) handling and rotation history for the last 36 months. Specifically our security team needs: 

- A chronological record of KEK rotations (timestamps, key IDs, operator IDs) for the last 36 months.
- Description of how KEKs are sealed/wrapped (HSM vendor, wrapping algorithm, KEK hierarchy).
- For hosted customers, confirmation of HSM-backed wrapping vs software wrapping, and for Private BYOK what handshake/proof exists.
- Tamper-evident audit trail proof (signed log entries or chain-of-trust) for rotation events.
- The last full keystore snapshot (metadata only, no private key material).
- A signed manufacturer attestation for the HSMs in use (or equivalent third-party attestation).

Can you provide an initial package and an ETA? If some items require an NDA or separate attestation process please flag. We prefer a combined ZIP with supporting CSV/JSON exports and a signed PDF attestation.

Thanks,
Laura
Security Assurance Lead
CrestBank

-----

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Laura Mills <laura.mills@crestbank.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: KEK sealing & rotation chronology

Laura / Kimberly — short technical summary and pointers (attaching rotation CSV and rotation-schedule):

1) Topology and wrapping
- Hosted Redwood API: KEKs are protected by HSM-wrapped master keys. For hosted tenants we use an HSM-backed key hierarchy (current deployments use AWS CloudHSM clusters for key wrapping). KEKs are never exported in plaintext; wrapping uses RSA-OAEP-SHA256 or AES-KW depending on HSM policy and tenant configuration.
- Private/BYOK deployments: customer may supply an HSM (PKCS#11 interface) or use a customer-managed CloudHSM. We record the BYOK handshake timestamp and the public key fingerprint in the tenant record.

2) Rotation practices
- Rotation cadence: KEKs are scheduled quarterly by default; emergency rotations trigger an immediate rolling rewrap of data keys with overlap to preserve availability.
- Overlap window: new KEK becomes active at t0; previous KEK remains valid for decrypt operations for 24 hours (configurable per tenant).
- Rotation metadata: CSV includes rotation_time_utc, old_key_id, new_key_id, requester, change_ticket_id. See attached rotation-schedule-2024-2027.csv.

3) Audit / tamper evidence
- Rotation operations are logged with signed entries. Each log entry is hashed and anchored to an append-only ledger service; per-rotation payloads include (rotation_time, key_ids, operator, signature).
- We can export the signed log bundle for the requested period. The export contains base64-encoded signed payloads (no secret material). Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/crestbank/kek-audit-extract-20270425

4) Attestation
- Attached: hsm-manufacturer-attestation-signed.pdf — a vendor-signed statement of HSM firmware and tamper features for the CloudHSM clusters we operate.
- If CrestBank requires an ISO/third-party-signed statement specific to your tenant, we can initiate the formal attestation flow (DocuSign route).

Let me know if you need the log bundle in a different format (JSONL vs CSV).

— Jonas Weber
Senior Crypto Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: rotation-schedule-2024-2027.csv, keystore-snapshot-20270420.json, hsm-manufacturer-attestation-signed.pdf

From: Laura Mills <laura.mills@crestbank.com>

Thanks Jonas/Kimberly — this is helpful. Quick follow-ups: 

- Can you confirm whether the signed log entries include a cryptographic signature tied to an internal signing key and whether that signing key has its own rotation history? We need to map chain-of-trust.
- Please redact any operator emails in the rotation CSV but keep operator-id and ticket references.
- For the HSM attestation PDF: can you provide a brief notes section that lists firmware version, FIPS level, and any tamper-event counters exposed?
- CrestBank policy requires a tenant-specific, signed attestation for production BYOK (we will provide the template if you can sign). Is that possible?

If you can cut a small addendum addressing the above, we can close this item in the SIG.

Best,
Laura

-----

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Laura Mills <laura.mills@crestbank.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-25T14:02:00-07:00

Laura — appreciate the clarifying questions. Short answers and next steps: 

- Signed log entries: yes — rotation logs are signed by an internal signing key (KeyID: rwd-sign-2021). That signing key itself is rotated annually; we will include the signing-key rotation table in the package (timestamps + key IDs, no private material). The signed log export will include the signature verifier material (public key) so you can validate chain-of-trust.
- Redaction: weve redacted operator emails in the CSV and retained operator_id and change_ticket_id as requested.
- Attestation notes: the attached HSM attestation includes firmware version, FIPS module statement, and tamper-event counter summary. See page 2 of the PDF for the quick table.
- Tenant-specific attestation: yes — we can sign CrestBanks template. Please send the template to security-requests@redwood.ai and well route for signature (or use the DocuSign link below).

Deliverables attached / links:
- keystore-snapshot-20270420.json (metadata only)
- rotation-schedule-2024-2027.csv (redacted operator emails)
- hsm-manufacturer-attestation-signed.pdf
- Signed log bundle (export link): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/crestbank/kek-audit-extract-20270425
- DocuSign attestation request (if preferred): https://docusign.com/msgs/xyz-attestation-crestbank

If you want a short executive summary for the SIG packet, Marissa can produce a one-page artifact that maps these files to typical SIG controls (CAIQ/SOC2 references). Marissa — can you pick that up?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Security Liaison | Redwood Inference
